patch.value: Add sparse lazy instances with a shared immutable object store

Materialize per-instance views over complete repository trees, fetch missing fragments lazily, and let independent working trees share immutable objects while retaining separate HEAD index view dirty state and operation logs.

A sparse view never changes committed tree identity and merges evaluate the complete tree; Out-of-view conflicts and incomplete PM attribution fail visibly rather than disappearing; Concurrent instances share immutable objects but cannot overwrite one another mutable state; A full scan reconciles dirty hints and filesystem state without trusting hints as authority

author: harness:codex
message: Keep Lore research only in linked PM records

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Starting implementation. Design: sparse linked instances over the hub's shared immutable store. Per-instance control directory holds HEAD, index (v4 with a sparse flag, git skip-worktree style), oplog, view.json, dirty-hint file and merge state; the hub keeps objects, refs, config and remotes shared (refs protected by existing compare-and-swap locks). Sparse index entries keep out-of-view content in every committed tree so a view can never change tree identity and merges always evaluate complete trees. Missing objects surface as typed missing_fragment errors with fetch remediation. Dirty hints are hints only: they can force extra verification, never suppress it; the full scan rewrites them from filesystem truth.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Regression proofs: each mutation was applied to the shipped code, its covering test observed failing (exit non-zero), and the mutation reverted; the full suite re-ran green after each revert. (1) materialize() drops sparse index entries -> 'a sparse view never changes committed tree identity' FAILS. (2) merge materializes out-of-view conflicts instead of refusing (outOfView forced empty) -> 'an out-of-view conflict fails visibly' FAILS. (3) commit accepts staged out-of-view changes (guard disabled) -> 'committing a staged change outside the view is refused' FAILS. (4) SharedObjectStore rethrows object_not_found untranslated -> 'a missing fragment is a typed, actionable error' FAILS. (5) instances open private stores/refs instead of the hub's -> concurrency test FAILS (shared store missing). (6) RefStore ignores headRoot so instances share HEAD -> concurrency test FAILS (HEAD overwritten). (7) scan() returns hinted paths instead of verified ones -> 'a full scan reconciles lying hints' FAILS. (8) status() stops passing hints as forced content checks -> the racy-stat adversarial case inside 'a full scan reconciles lying hints' FAILS (the forged-stat edit reads clean without the hint).

patch.value: Implemented sparse lazy instances over the shared immutable store: per-instance HEAD/index/view/oplog/hints, shared objects/refs/config, index v4 sparse entries preserving tree identity, visible out-of-view and attribution failures, typed missing_fragment errors, locked instance registry, filesystem-authoritative scan. All 8 regression mutations proven failing; release:check green with 594 tests at 100% coverage.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: CodeRabbit review round on PR 32, ten findings. Five Major adopted: the registry lock reported every openSync errno as a held lock when only EEXIST means that; the dirty-hint filter was quadratic in hints times index entries and now intersects through a set; linkInstance could create a shared branch and then fail materialization, stranding a branch with no instance, and now undoes only what it created and only while the compare-and-swap still shows it as ours; the view-change loop mutated the working tree one path at a time so a mid-loop throw left the tree and index disagreeing, and now plans first by reading every widened object and rejecting a narrowed path that holds a directory before the first byte moves; and ScanReport.checked counted absent paths it never read, which contradicted its own documented meaning, now corrected in the code, the doc and two tests. Three minor adopted: a redundant null check after an early return, an unrestored directory mode in a test that leaked an unremovable temp directory when the awaited command rejected, and a per-path view.json read inside the out-of-view conflict filter now hoisted. Two declined with reasons recorded on the PR threads.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: A defect the review did not find, surfaced by chasing the last uncovered branch. The rollback's cleanup target was chosen by createdRoot ? instanceRoot : instanceControl, and the second arm had no test because no test had ever linked an instance into a directory the caller supplied. Writing that test failed at once: the rollback removed the control directory but left materialized working-tree files behind, so a caller who handed over an empty directory got it back holding partial content from a creation that never completed. That contradicts the rollback's own stated contract of undoing only what the call did, since the materialized files are exactly what the call did. When the caller supplied the directory the rollback now clears its contents rather than only the control directory, which is precisely correct because the pre-flight refuses a non-empty directory, so everything inside it at cleanup time was written by this call. Reverting to the control-directory-only cleanup fails the new test. Worth recording the shape: the uncovered branch was uncovered because the path it guarded had never been exercised, and that path was broken.
